A new framework called Fed-Equilibrium aims to address issues in Federated Learning within clinical networks, particularly the problem of knowledge dominance where larger centers overshadow smaller cohorts. This framework enhances efficiency and fairness by implementing a two-stage gradient control system, ensuring that minority contributions are given equal importance in data processing. Experiments demonstrate that this approach allows underrepresented clinical signals to achieve convergence comparable to data-rich centers, promoting equitable data sharing across networks.

 - Fed-Equilibrium addresses knowledge dominance in Federated Learning.
 - The framework utilizes a two-stage gradient control system for improved data fairness.
 - Experimental results show that minority clinical data can achieve convergence similar to that of larger data-rich hubs.

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.11937
